title: Three unix tests have weak or unverified oracles
description:
All three found by the test-integrity lens:

1. unix.rs:205 the_resolved_name_matches_id asserts id -un succeeded. On a host where the running uid has no passwd entry (container run with --user 1234:1234, distroless CI) id -un exits nonzero and the test fails -- reporting a defect in code behaving exactly as username_for's doc comment specifies. Give it the integration test's two-branch shape.

2. tests/unix_account_live.rs:60 oracle_display_name returns format!("uid {uid}") when id -un fails -- byte-for-byte the literal at unix.rs:146. The test then compares the implementation's fallback against a hand-copied duplicate of that same fallback, and getpwuid_r is never compared to anything external. Green having exercised no lookup, with no signal to the reader. Split the fallback expectation into its own named test.

3. unix.rs:213 asserts username_for(4_000_000_000) == None on the bare premise that nothing maps that uid. Against an LDAP backend with a wide range the premise is false. id -un 4000000000 is the same oracle the sibling test already trusts and costs one subprocess.
